title: The nine reconciliations name one Workbench side, but that side sits in seven service schemas
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
section: Reconciliations (note A2 and REC-01 to REC-09)
description: Version 3 says each reconciliation compares ACE, read through a v_ace_* view, with the case list or the Workbench record it feeds, and names one run for all nine. In the target a service owns its schema and no service reads another service table, so one JOB-04 run cannot read the rwb_case, rwb_treatment, rwb_payment, rwb_comms, rwb_writeoff, rwb_asset or rwb_decision rows that form the Workbench side of REC-01 to REC-08. The sheet has no owner column and no per-service split.
evidence: v3 Reconciliations!A2 (Each compares ACE ... with the case list or the Workbench record it feeds) and B5:G13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheets Services (19 services, one schema and one login each) and Tables (recovery_case P3, treatment S2, proceeds P8, notice P6, write_off S7, asset_sale S5, decision_log_entry P7); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 1079 and line 2884 (P1 owns the ACE view contract, freshness and reconciliation), line 2980 (JOB-04 owner rwb-source-data) and line 2903 (one schema and one login per service); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11; ADR-014.
proposed: Every reconciliation row gets an owner from the Ownership Map: the service that holds the Workbench side answers it on its contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and rwb-source-data keeps the ACE side and the JOB-04 run.

title: No reconciliation and no quality measure carries an owner
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 names no service and no owner on any of the nine reconciliations and on any of the six quality measures. The break route names business roles only (data steward, officer, Credit Administration, Head of NPA, platform administrator). The target gives every table an owner in the Ownership Map and every service its own schema and login, so the missing owner is the one value that decides who runs and answers each check.
evidence: v3 Reconciliations!A4:G4 (ID, Source side, Workbench side, Compared on, Tolerance, When, Break goes to) and Quality measures!A4:C4 (Measure, Meaning, Target) with no owner column; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (93 rows, every table with an owner) and sheet Services; Template and Rules R4 (schema rwb_<short>, login per service) and R5.3 (suggested owner by team type); ADR-014; DL46.
proposed: Two columns are appended to Reconciliations (Owner, Per-service reconciliation) and one to Quality measures (Owner service), every value taken from the Ownership Map sheet Tables and every cell named for a service and its schema.

title: REC-08 compares a decision-log copy that the target retires
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
description: REC-08 compares a decision-log copy with the live decision log, on count and last hash, nightly. That copy is the copy to the data lake, and the data lake is removed: RWB-E1-014 is retired, JOB-13 is now a continuous Kafka ingest into rwb-decision, and JOB-14 runs the hash-chain check at 02:00. The row therefore compares a population that no longer exists against a ledger that is now the central record of all 19 services.
evidence: v3 Reconciliations!B12 (Decision log copy) and C12 (Live decision log); Template and Rules R6 (RWB-E1-014 decision log copy to the data lake retired: no data lake in Arch v5); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2881 (P7 owns approvals, the central decision ledger and the DMN model registry), line 2920 (DecisionRecorded from all 19 on rwb.decision-record.v1), line 2988 (JOB-13 Decision log copy, ingest is continuous by Kafka) and line 2989 (JOB-14 Hash-chain check 02:00); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03.
proposed: REC-08 compares the local decision record of each of the 19 services on rwb.decision-record.v1 with the central decision_log_entry of P7, still on count and last hash, nightly, with the 02:00 hash-chain check.

title: No per-service reconciliation rule, cadence or result route
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 holds nine central rows only. It has no row per service, no cadence for a service outside the ACE chain (the document intake, the file windows, the agent runs, the partner results) and no route by which a service hands its result to reconciliation_result, which the Ownership Map gives to rwb-source-data. The target needs all three for the 19 services, because each one owns rows that no other service can read.
evidence: v3 Reconciliations!A4:G13 (nine rows, no service row and no result route); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables row reconciliation_result (P1) and the other 92 rows with their owners; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2884 (P1 owns reconciliation) and line 2980 (JOB-04 Reconciliation, event-triggered workflow on rwb-source-data), line 2987 (JOB-12 Document intake every 15 min), line 2985 (JOB-10 WIN notices 16:00); Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-09; ADR-014.
proposed: A Per-service reconciliation sheet gives one row per service with its tables, the part of each check it runs, the key, the tolerance, the cadence, the break and result route, the pattern and the basis; where the source states no cadence or result route the cell carries the placeholder of Template and Rules R9.

title: Ten services have no tolerance and no legacy reconciliation row
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
description: The nine reconciliations name P1, P3, S2, P8, P6, S7, S5 and P7. Ten services own tables and appear in no reconciliation row at all: P2, P4, P5, P10, S1, S3, S4, S6, S8 and S9. The source states no tolerance for any of them, and no business value may be invented for it.
evidence: v3 Reconciliations!A5:A13 (REC-01 to REC-09 name P1, P3, S2, P8, P6, S7, S5 and P7 only); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows for the ten owners (P2 interface_config, job_catalog, outbound_item; P4 role, permission, role_conflict, delegation_limit, masking_rule; P5 document, document_intake, document_text and the other document tables; P10 the eight agent tables; S3 guarantee_claim; S4 legal_action, hearing; S6 debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account; S8 deviation; S9 partner, partner_user, partner_instruction) and no S1 row; Template and Rules R9 (placeholder and candidate row).
proposed: The tolerance cell of those ten rows carries the placeholder of Template and Rules R9; a value is a business decision for Step D1 and is not set here.

title: REC-05 and REC-09 are numbered the other way round from RWB-E1-011
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 numbers the notice-barcode check REC-05 and the business-key orphan check REC-09. RWB-E1-011 and every realigned slice number the business-key check REC-05 and the notice-barcode check REC-09, so a story or a screen that cites REC-05 can mean either check. Both documents describe the same two checks; only the number of each is transposed.
evidence: v3 Reconciliations!A9:G9 (REC-05 Notices sent to WIN against Barcodes returned in recovery.v_ace_pod) and A13:G13 (REC-09 Every account_key, person_key, asset_key and payment_code against the matching view row); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 011 Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md line 47 (REC-05 resolves every account_key ...) and line 155 (BR5 REC-05); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P6 rwb-comms (Communications)/RWB P6 E1011 APP Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md line 43 and line 192 (the collision is recorded there as CG-B-P6-04-E1011-3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E1011 APP Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md line 203 (REC-05 is the business-key check); Template and Rules R8.2 and root rule 8.
proposed: v4 keeps the source IDs and adds a REC numbering block that maps each check to the number this document gives it and the number RWB-E1-011 and the story set give it; Step D1 aligns the two on one numbering and no ID is renumbered here.

title: S1 rwb-valuation owns no table in the Ownership Map
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Arch v5 gives rwb-valuation the valuations, the D6 route decision and the route agent output, and Temporal gives it RouteDecisionWorkflow. The Ownership Map sheet Tables holds 93 tables and not one of them is owned by S1, so a per-service reconciliation for rwb-valuation has no table to run on.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2892 (S1 rwb-valuation owns valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output, schema rwb_valuation) and line 1865 (RouteDecisionWorkflow on rwb-valuation); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Services row S1 (schema rwb_valuation) and sheet Tables (93 rows, no S1 owner); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13 (RouteDecisionWorkflow); Template and Rules R9 (placeholder).
proposed: The S1 row keeps rwb-valuation as the owner, states the capability Arch v5 gives it and carries the placeholder of Template and Rules R9 until the Ownership Map lists a table for it.

title: REC-03 and REC-04 have no per-service owner in the RWB-E1-011 slice set
description: The treatments check REC-03 reads rwb_treatment and the payments check REC-04 reads rwb_payment, so the Workbench side of each belongs to S2 and P8. The RWB-E1-011 slices are P1, P3, S5, P6, the P1 OPS story and the ITG harness: there is no S2 slice and no P8 slice, and the ITG run reports both checks NOT_RUN until those services land. The capability therefore has no per-service owner even though its tables do.
evidence: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy RWB-E1-011 slices (RWB-P1-E1011-APP, RWB-P3-E1011-APP, RWB-S5-E1011-APP, RWB-P6-E1011-APP, RWB-P1-E1011-OPS, RWB-P1-E1011-CON, RWB-ITG-E1011-ITG); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data (Source data)/RWB P1 E1011 APP Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md section 1 (REC-03 and REC-04 are not P1 slices); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W1 Wave 1 integration/RWB ITG E1011 ITG Reconciliation and data quality report - integration v1.md section 4 step 7 and AC12 (REC-03 and REC-04 report NOT_RUN until rwb-treatment and rwb-payment land); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (treatment S2, proceeds P8).
proposed: S2 and P8 own the Workbench side of REC-03 and REC-04 and answer it on their contracts; a slice for each is added at Step D1. This document records the per-service split now and does not create a story.

title: The Timeliness measure reads a Workbench read of the ACE batch that no service but P1 makes
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Quality and Reconciliation Rules v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 defines Timeliness as the ACE batch for the business date being complete when the Workbench reads it. Only rwb-source-data holds the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and publishes AceDataReady; every other service reads the freshness contract, so the measure as written describes a read that no other service makes and gives no owner for the measure itself.
evidence: v3 Quality measures!B7 (The ACE batch for the business date is complete when the Workbench reads it); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 1081 (P1 SQL ACE DB views: SELECT recovery.v_ace_* 30 views), line 1115 (P1 OUT: ACE view contract and freshness), line 2294 (AceDataReady starts the morning run of the other services) and line 2341 and line 2342 (POST /v1/business-days/{date}/ready is idempotent and Airflow never reads or writes rwb_* schemas); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05; ADR-014.
proposed: Timeliness reads: the ACE batch for the business date is complete when rwb-source-data reads it and publishes AceDataReady; every other service measures the freshness contract, and the measure carries P1 rwb-source-data as its owner.
